decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “Add ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client confirms: “Saving a link and having it stick when I reload also works.”
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: the presented save capability conforms to saving a bookmark by URL.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents only “Add ... bookmarks”; Round 2 maker later says metadata fetching was newly “Implemented.” Round 1 client identifies the initial behavior: “I still have to type the title myself” and requests that a pasted URL “grabs the page's title and a short description.”
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: automatic title and description collection was missing. The client explicitly identifies the mismatch and supplies the reference-conforming behavior.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: “edit ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client offers only the broad response, “Everything else about how I add, organize, and find things is good.”
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: the presentation does not identify which bookmark fields are editable, so conformity or divergence for URL, title, description, tags, and note cannot be established. The broad approval does not resolve it.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker explicitly includes “delete ... bookmarks.” The Round 1 client requests no change to deletion.
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: the recorded deletion decision conforms to the reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “archive ... bookmarks.” Round 1 client says they tried “archiving” and it behaved as desired, but does not state whether archived items are retained and excluded from the default list and ordinary search.
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: archive is present, but its required hide-while-retaining semantics are not established. Bare approval does not supply the missing detail.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists “delete” and “archive” as separate actions. The client approves archiving generally but does not address whether archive is reversible and deletion permanent.
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: the actions are distinguished nominally, but the reference-required lifecycle distinction cannot be established.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents “Search.” Round 1 client says “I tried searching ... [and it] behave[s] the way I'd want”; Round 2 maker only adds that the saved bookmark “remained searchable.”
decisions.note: Implementation review: neither presentation establishes whether search covers title, description, note, and URL. The client's generic approval does not clarify that scope.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “tag filtering.” Round 1 client reports “filtering by a tag ... behave[s] the way I'd want.”
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: tag-based filtering is a functionally conforming presentation.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes “sorting.” Round 1 client reports trying “sorting” and says it behaves as desired.
decisions.note: Initial implementation review: the presented ability to sort the bookmark list conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “The page title and description are fetched automatically.” Round 2 client verifies that “the title and description fill themselves in.”
decisions.note: Revised implementation review: the title-and-description portion of automatic metadata collection now conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker's announced fetched metadata lists only “title and description,” omitting the required favicon and preview image. Round 2 client discusses only title and description and concludes, “I'm happy with it.”
decisions.note: Revised implementation review: the metadata implementation remains incomplete because favicon and preview-image collection are absent from the presented fetch scope. The client does not state that expectation or identify the difference; general approval is insufficient.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes bookmark editing; Round 2 maker says the fetched title and description “remain editable.” Round 2 client confirms, “I could still edit both before saving.”
decisions.note: Revised implementation review: taken together, the presentations retain editing for the automatically populated title and description before saving and expose bookmark editing afterward.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: “If metadata is unavailable, saving still works using the domain as a fallback title.” Round 2 client tests a made-up address and confirms it “still let me save using the site name.”
decisions.note: Revised implementation review: URL-only saving remains possible even when metadata lookup fails.
